S34.01.note: Ctrl+F/Cmd+F is wired in apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ChatMessageList.tsx; the jump-to-match logic was not fully read.
steps: Open a conversation that has several messages.
Press Command+F.
Type a word that appears in an earlier message.
Look for the "N of M matches" count beside the box.
Press Enter or use the "Next match" arrow to jump between matches, then compare with Expected.
S34.01.where: Open any chat > press Command+F (Ctrl+F on Windows) > type in "Search messages..."

S34.02.needs: a conversation with a known word in its text
S34.02.note: Which conversations are visible is decided by the server in apps/web/app/api/search/route.ts; the UI cannot show that rule.
steps: Click "Search" in the sidebar, or press Command+Shift+F.
Type a word from a past conversation title or message.
Wait for the results list.
Click a matching conversation result.
Check that the conversation opens and the result matches Expected.
S34.02.where: Sidebar > Search > type in "Search your workspace"

S34.03.needs: a Free account or paid account with at least one project
S34.03.note: The category chips were taken from the shared category list; the exact chip rendering was not read line by line.
steps: Click "Search" in the sidebar, or press Command+Shift+F.
Type the name of one of your projects.
Click the "Projects" category chip.
Click the matching project result.
Check that the project opens and the match is by name or description.
S34.03.where: Sidebar > Search > type a project name > category "Projects"

S34.04.needs: a file already saved in the Library
S34.04.note: The placeholder says files and projects; the Expected line says name or prompt. Whether prompts are matched was not confirmed in the UI code.
steps: Click "Library" in the sidebar.
Click in the box "Search files and projects".
Type part of a saved file name.
Check that the list narrows to matching items.
Clear the box and check the full list returns.
S34.04.where: Sidebar > Library > type in "Search files and projects"

S34.05.note: The artifacts route at apps/web/app/chat/artifacts/page.tsx was not walked; content matching was not confirmed.
steps: Click "Library" in the sidebar.
Choose the "Artifacts" view.
Click the search box and type part of an artifact title.
Check that only matching artifacts remain.
Open a matching artifact and compare with Expected.
S34.05.where: Sidebar > Library > Artifacts > type in "Search files and projects"

S34.06.needs: a connected work source such as Google Drive or Slack
S34.06.note: The exact button that opens the Connectors menu was not confirmed; the search itself runs on the server.
steps: Open a chat and find the Connectors control in the message box.
Open the "Connectors" menu.
Check which connected sources are listed and enabled.
Send a question that asks about a connected source, for example a Drive or Slack file.
Look for the answer to use that source, and compare with Expected.

S34.07.needs: a model that supports web search
S34.07.note: The on/off control for Web search was not confirmed; the /search command is handled at ChatComposerNew.tsx line 3190.
steps: Open a chat and look at the message box options.
Turn on "Web search" if it is offered, or type /search followed by a question.
Send a question about a current event.
Look for an answer that cites web sources.
Compare with Expected.

S34.15.needs: conversations dated across more than one range
S34.15.note: The button that reveals the filter fields was not confirmed; the date fields are present in the dialog code.
steps: Click "Search" in the sidebar.
Open the filter area of the search dialog.
Click the "From Date" box and choose a start date, then "To Date" and choose an end date.
Type a word and search.
Check that every result date falls inside the chosen range.
S34.15.where: Sidebar > Search > (filter area) > From Date / To Date

labels.text: Search sources by name or summary

S34.19.note: The project Sources panel exists, but no control was found for putting chosen sources into a named collection or limiting chats to it. Searched the project files for collection and knowledge controls; only the Sources panel and its search box were found.

S34.20.needs: some earlier searches so the recent list is not empty
S34.20.note: The heading for the popular list was not read, so only the Recent Searches heading is confirmed.
steps: Click "Search" in the sidebar.
Leave the search box empty and look below it.
Check for the "Recent Searches" list and the popular list.
Click one suggestion.
Check that it fills the box and runs the search.

S34.21.needs: a paid account or a setting turned on
S34.21.note: Follow-up suggestions are off by default (FOLLOW_UP_SUGGESTIONS_ENABLED_DEFAULT = false in apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ChatMessageList.tsx) and depend on a settings flag; the Settings screen that sets it was not found.

S34.22.needs: none, but the assistant decides whether to ask
S34.22.note: The card appears only when the assistant decides to ask; there is no control to force it, so the tester may not see it.
steps: Open a chat and send a vague request that a clarification would help with.
Wait for a card that asks questions.
Pick one of the offered choices, or type in "Something else…".
Click "Send answers".
Check that the search runs after the answers are sent.
S34.22.where: Chat > the reply card with "Send answers"

S34.23.needs: content in the workspace that matches a word
S34.23.note: The result-row markup was not read line by line; the citation preview is in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/CitationChip.tsx.
steps: Click "Search" in the sidebar.
Type a word and press Enter.
Look at each result row for a title and a short text line.
Hover a citation chip inside an answer and compare its preview with Expected.
S34.23.where: Sidebar > Search > type a word > a result row

steps: Send a question that uses web search.
Wait for the answer, then click the "Sources" button under it.
Look at the source panel that opens.
Check each source card shows a title, a site line and a link.
S34.24.where: Chat > answer with web sources > "Sources" button under the answer

S34.25.needs: a web search answer with citations; a mouse for hover (tap on touch)
S34.25.note: The preview tooltip is in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/CitationChip.tsx but its visible words are generated from the source, so no fixed label was found.
steps: Send a question that returns cited web sources.
Move the mouse over a citation chip in the answer.
Check that a preview appears with the source title, site and snippet.
Move the mouse away and check the answer is still in place.
S34.25.where: Chat > answer with citations > hover a citation chip

S34.26.needs: a web search answer with more than three sources
S34.26.note: The expand-to-full-list behaviour uses the research panel store; the exact expand control was not separately confirmed.
steps: Open a web search answer.
Click the "Sources" button under it.
Look for the summary count on the button, for example "Sources · 5".
Check that the panel lists the "Citations" section and, if present, the "More" section.
S34.26.where: Chat > answer with web sources > "Sources" button > "Citations" and "More" headings

S34.27.note: Source cards open the URL in a new tab (target _blank); a citation chip link does the same in CitationChip.tsx.
steps: Open a web search answer and click the "Sources" button.
Click a source card title.
Check that the original page opens in a new tab.
S34.27.where: Chat > answer with web sources > "Sources" button > click a source title

S34.31.note: The publish date is shown only when the search provider returns one (apps/web/lib/web-search/web-search-tool.ts).
steps: Open a web search answer and click the "Sources" button.
Read the small grey line under a source title.
Check it shows a publish date when known and "Retrieved" followed by a date.
S34.31.where: Chat > answer with web sources > "Sources" button > a source row subtitle

S34.32.note: The unavailable-source text is in apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx near line 3657; reproducing a failed search needs a network or provider fault.
steps: Click "Search" in the sidebar.
Type a made-up word such as xqzvk and press Enter.
Look for the empty-state text.
Open a chat answer with no web results and look for the notice that the answer used the model's own knowledge.
S34.32.where: Sidebar > Search > type a nonsense word > "No results found"
